1.title: Understand what clients need from financial services
1.intro: Clients seek planning, tax, insurance, credit and investing advice.
pts: Know the service lines and who can offer each.
Interview five clients on their goals and worries.
Choose a niche such as newcomers, students or small businesses.
Write a service sheet.
Separate education from advice: explaining a savings account differs from recommending a product; check the provincial rule on what needs registration.
Ask what worries each client most and record it in their own words.
List what you will not do and where you refer those clients.
1.ex: Newcomers need credit history, tax filing and savings plans in their first year. A newcomer who earns 3,000 a month and saves 300 has a savings rate of 300 / 3,000 = 10%, a starting point for a plan.
1.act: Interview five people and write a service sheet.

2.title: Know registration and conduct rules
pts: Provincial securities, insurance and mortgage regulators license advisers.
Know-your-client and suitability duties usually require documented advice; check the rule that applies to your registration.
Anti-money-laundering rules require identifying clients and reporting suspicious activity; check which apply to your registration.
Privacy law covers client records.
Write a one-page conduct code covering honesty, disclosure and putting the client first.
Know when to refer: complex tax, legal questions, or products outside your registration.
Store client records securely and keep them for the period the regulator requires; check the provincial rule.
2.ex: Row: 'Recommend a fund | provincial securities regulator | registration and suitability record | each advice | file note'. A second row: 'Share client data | privacy law | written consent | before sharing | consent form'. Date each source.
2.std: Cite a source and a date for every row.

3.title: Build a plan and explain it
pts: Collect the client's goals, income, costs, debts and assets.
Compute net worth and savings rate.
Set action steps with dates.
Explain the risks and fees in the plan in plain words.
Compute net worth as assets minus debts for the fictional client.
Build a monthly budget with income, fixed costs, flexible costs and savings.
Set an emergency fund target of three months of costs.
3.ex: Income 4,000, costs 3,200; savings are 800 and the savings rate is 800 / 4,000 = 20%. Three months of costs is 3 x 3,200 = 9,600, which takes 9,600 / 800 = 12 months to save.
3.act: Build a plan for a fictional client.

4.title: Price the service
pts: Choose a fee model: hourly, fixed or percentage; check the provincial rule on what your registration allows.
Disclose all costs and fees to the client in writing before work starts.
Track your time on each client file.
Work out break-even hours as fixed cost divided by margin per hour.
Compare fee models: 20 hours at 150 is 3,000, against a fixed fee of 2,800.
Write a fee schedule that lists what is included.
Track time in 15-minute blocks and review the price each quarter.
4.ex: Fee 150 per hour; cost 25; margin 125; fixed cost 3,000 a month gives 3,000 / 125 = 24 hours. At 20 billable hours the margin is 20 x 125 = 2,500, which is 500 short. Teaching figures in CAD.

5.title: Run records and reviews
pts: Keep a checklist for every client file.
Review each client's plan every year.
Have a written complaints process.
Arrange supervision or peer review of your files.
Make a client-file checklist and tick each item.
Put the annual review date in the file and the calendar.
Write complaint steps: acknowledge, investigate, answer in writing.
5.ex: Audit of five mock files: 4 had suitability notes, 1 did not, so 80% were complete. After the checklist was introduced, 5 of 5 (100%) had notes.

6.title: Win clients ethically
pts: Win clients through referrals and community talks.
Publish free guides in plain language.
End every contact with a clear next step.
Track talks, meetings and clients.
Give a talk to a community group on one topic, such as a first tax filing, without selling a product.
Offer a free first meeting of 30 minutes with a written agenda.
Send a written summary within two days.
6.ex: Funnel: 30 talks, 8 meetings, 3 clients. Meeting rate is 8 / 30 = 27%, client rate is 3 / 8 = 37.5%, and overall 3 / 30 = 10%.

7.title: Manage conflict, fraud and market risk
pts: Disclose conflicts of interest before giving advice.
Learn the signs of fraud and what to do when you see them.
Never promise investment returns.
Have a business continuity plan.
Teach clients common scams: urgent payment demands, gift-card requests and promised returns; tell them to verify by calling a known number.
Write a conflict disclosure statement in plain words.
Plan continuity: back up files and name a person to call if you are away.
7.ex: Risk: 'Client scam loss | 3 x 5 | warnings and verification | adviser | quarterly'. The score is 3 x 5 = 15, so it is high priority and reviewed every quarter.
7.std: Name an owner for each item.

8.title: Pilot with mock clients
8.intro: Practise on fictional clients before you advise real ones.
pts: Run the pilot with mock clients only, with no real client money or advice.
Have a peer review each plan.
Stop rule: a plan with missing disclosure fails and must be fixed.
Reflect on what the reviews showed and write one lesson.
Prepare three fictional clients with different incomes, such as 2,500, 4,000 and 6,000 a month.
Ask a peer to play the client and raise a hard question about fees.
Score each plan against a ten-item checklist.
8.ex: All three plans passed the disclosure check, which is 3 of 3 (100%). Had one failed, the stop rule says to fix it before any real client.

quiz: Advice fitting the client's goals, risk and situation.
Provincial regulators, and in some cases federal bodies; check which applies.
What is a conflict of interest?
A situation where your gain may clash with the client's.
What triggers fail in the mock?
